Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

away from preposition

classical

Gell. 15.7.3: cum ā mē abes
Catull. 46.10: ā domō profectōs

ā, ab (+ ablative)

preposition with the ablative; ā before consonants, ab before vowels and h

Separation and distance: ā mē abesse, be away from me. With names of towns, domus and rūs prose uses the ablative alone (domō abesse); verse may add ā. The prefix ab- says it in the verb: abīre, go away (see away).

Other words

  • procul (ab + ablative) — far away from

    adverb; with ab + ablative, or the ablative alone in verse · also used · classical · Hor. Epod. 2.1: procul negōtiīs; Cic. Off. 1.136: īra procul absit

    Far off, out of the way: procul ab urbe; alone, as a command, procul!, away! (see far).

Examples

  • avē, mī Gāī, meus asellus jūcundissimus, quem semper medius fidius dēsīderō, cum ā mē abes

    greetings, my Gaius, my dearest little donkey, whom I always miss, so help me, when you are away from meGell. 15.7.3

  • longē quōs simul ā domō profectōs dīversae variē viae reportant

    who set out together far away from home, and whom different roads bring back by different waysCatull. 46.10–11

  • beātus ille quī procul negōtiīs, ut prīsca gēns mortālium

    happy the man who, far away from business, like the first race of mortals …Hor. Epod. 2.1–2

  • pōma sumus Cybelēs: procul hinc discēde, viātor, nē cadat in miserum nostra ruīna caput

    we are Cybele’s fruit: get well away from here, traveller, or we may fall on your poor headMart. 13.25.1–2

  • sed tamen īra procul absit, cum quā nihil rēctē fierī, nihil cōnsīderātē potest

    but let anger be far away, for with it nothing can be done rightly or with thoughtCic. Off. 1.136

See also from, away, away, far.
